title: Make the Exorcist Fall in Love Manga Starts Final Arc
content:
The wraparound jacket band for the 16th compiled book volume of writer Aruma Arima and artist Masuku Fukayama 's Make the Exorcist Fall in Love ( Exorcist o Otosenai ) manga revealed the start of the manga's final arc. The volume shipped on Wednesday.

Shueisha 's MANGA Plus service publishes the manga in English and describes the story:

A boy was chosen by god to become the world's strongest exorcist and to face deadly demons in battle. Burdened with the fate of humanity, all he really wants to do is quietly bake sweets, when one day a certain girl enters his life... A story of love and hope blooming during a bloody holy war!

Arima and Fukayama launched the manga on Shueisha 's Shonen Jump+ website in 2021.

title: Crunchyroll’s New Solo Leveling Replacement Delivers a Surprisingly Deep Portrayal of Men’s Emotions
content:
Crunchyroll ‘s Overgeared , the Fall 2026 replacement for Solo Leveling , surprisingly depicts the perfect emotional complexity of men in a single episode. Many anime based on Korean webtoons or featuring a protagonist who levels up are often dubbed the next Solo Leveling . This is especially true this year, as multiple anime have emerged that could fill the void left by its absence. It started with Tomb Raider King in Summer 2026, which was surprisingly similar to Solo Leveling . Now, in Fall 2026, two anime have emerged with similar elements. However, Overgeared , another adaptation of a Korean webtoon, serves as a sort of replacement for Solo Leveling .

But Overgeared doesn’t just incorporate the elements that make Solo Leveling such a cool anime. It adds its own nuances and, notably, takes a hilarious twist. The series features Grid, a protagonist desperate to level up in life, earn money, and provide for his loved ones. However, the difference is that Grid’s desperation is portrayed in a humorous way. In the fifth episode of Overgeared , the series takes a turn in Grid’s life. While it hilariously depicts how he now has a better life, there is also a hidden emotional complexity that men experience, which Grid’s situation perfectly highlights.

Crunchyroll’s Fall 2026 Solo Leveling Replacement Hides Men’s Emotional Complexity Beneath Its Hilarious Surface

Ever since the first episode of the series , Grid has been portrayed as a protagonist deemed a failure and desperate to earn enough money to get by and contribute to his family. With the new opportunity presented to him, the last few episodes have seen him upgrade his crafting skills, and after securing a deal within the Satisfy game, he was finally able to generate enough money. By creating a legendary weapon, Grid managed to sell it for a price equivalent to 24.8 million yen in real life, finally giving him the confidence and relief he had been seeking. More importantly, however, is how his family reacts to his situation.

Until he brought in money, his family treated him as nothing more than a burden, with the episode hilariously depicting them as having only one child: Grid’s sister. As soon as Grid reveals that he has earned money and can contribute to paying off the family’s debt, with plans to clear it entirely in the future, he is suddenly considered an important member of the family. All of this is hilariously depicted, but on a deeper level, it highlights the reality of men, which has always remained the same regardless of class or country. The ability to provide for one’s loved ones has long been tied to the definition of being a man, and, albeit hilariously, Overgeared portrays this through Grid.

Grid has arguably become one of the most relatable protagonists, as his emotional displays and the desperation of a 25-year-old man trying to succeed in life feel incredibly realistic, especially for those in the same age group who fear what the future holds. The protagonist is honestly what makes Overgeared stand out, even as it is frequently referred to as Solo Leveling ‘s replacement because of their shared elements. It is a different kind of Solo Leveling replacement on Crunchyroll , and its portrayal of men’s emotional complexity, though hilarious on the surface, is also poignant upon closer inspection.

title: Martial Arts Manhwa Artist Seung-nam Ha Dies at 68
content:
Born in Busan in 1958, Ha entered the comics industry as an apprentice to artist Nam-gil Heo. He made his debut in 1980 with The King of Baseball Without a Nationality .

One of his best-known works, Goltong's Declaration of Departure , began serialization in the newspaper Sports Today in 2001. The comic follows Yoo Se-ok, a young man who enters the martial arts world at his master's command and becomes involved in a series of chaotic adventures. Ha founded Ha Seung-nam Production the following year and continued publishing works in the Goltong series featuring Yoo. He was also known for Divine Sword and Evil Sword .

Ha also pursued opportunities overseas. He serialized comics in the Taiwanese comics magazine Infinite Boys in 1994 and published Sayaka in 2004 and Existence in 2005 in Japanese manga magazines. He was also the artist for the Records of the Three Kingdoms manga. In 2007, he became the first Korean comic artist to join the Japan Cartoonists Association as a full member. Ha served as a board member of the Korea Cartoonist Association.

title: Controversial Shonen Jump Creator Breaks Silence on Series Finale
content:
Drama Queen is ending after only two years, and the creator clarified a major misconception. December 2024 was a most controversial time for Shueisha’s Shonen Jump+ platform when the release of this manga. Written and illustrated by Kuraku Ichikawa, the series grabbed attention for all the wrong reasons when readers weren’t happy about the plot and setting of the story. While many defended the story, the majority of the readers were disappointed with the introduction. This is the major reason why the series remained controversial throughout its run. However, this controversy is the reason why Drama Quee n gained so much popularity , enough to rank in the top charts of the Manga Plus app.

Before the series could even be serialized for two years, it announced its finale, which will end in December this year, considering there are no delays. The series has released 73 chapters so far, and it will wrap up after releasing four more chapters. The sudden finale and a weekly serialization of only two years led many to believe that the series is being canceled rather than coming to a more conclusive finale. Considering how common it is in Shonen Jump for series to be cancelled in the first few months or even a couple of years, the rumors weren’t surprising. However, Ichikawa shares a special message to fans while also clearing up the misunderstanding.

Drama Queen Creator Breaks Silence on Manga Finale

In their official X handle , Ichikawa shared, “Four episodes left until the finale. Thanks to everyone, I was able to draw everything I wanted to. From here, there are about two more developments, and various things will connect. Look forward to it.” The creator specifically mentioned that they were able to proceed with the story and draw everything they wanted to. This not only means that the cancellation rumors were false, but also that the series was always meant to be considerably shorter.

Drama Queen is Ichikawa’s first serialized manga, which, for better or worse, became extremely popular . Before the serialization, the creator worked on a couple of one-shots, none of which gained as much attention as this one. The story has had its ups and downs throughout the serialization, but Ichikawa promises to wrap up the story after answering the questions that will connect all the loose ends.

What Is the Drama Queen Controversy?

The series encountered racist allegations for its alleged anti-immigrant themes. Additionally, many readers believed that one dialogue was a jab at the LGBTQ+ community due to the way it described the word “partner,” which is why Shueisha had to quietly edit that scene. The story takes place in modern Japan, nine years after the aliens saved Earth from destruction and moved there. While the aliens are hailed as the saviors, Nomamoto, a factory worker, sees the race for who they are. After a chance encounter with Kitami, a young man who lost his family because of these aliens, Nomamoto’s seemingly mundane life turns upside down. It doesn’t take long for the story to take a dark turn.

The very first chapter features Nomamoto and Kitami cooking the alien and eating him. Nomamoto mentions that the smell of the aliens burning smells awfully similar to squid, a popular seafood delicacy. Several readers interpreted the depiction of aliens as a metaphor for immigrants or foreigners, leading to discussions about potential racism or xenophobia in the story, while some defended that fiction should be taken as merely fiction and that the manga is being misinterpreted. They suggested that the aliens are not intended to represent immigrants but rather serve as a plot device, but that did very little to quell the controversy.

What are your thoughts on the Drama Queen manga? Head down to the comments to let us know if you’ve been keeping up with the series after its initial surge in popularity.

title: Avatar: Seven Havens Producers Confirm Asami’s Fate Ahead of Season 2
content:
Avatar: Seven Havens has wrapped up its first season, and the producers behind it all have clarified Asami’s fate ahead of Season 2. Avatar: Seven Havens picks up hundreds of years after the events of The Legend of Korra , so many fans had been wondering what kind of connection could be seen with its predecessor, if there were any connections at all. But towards the end of the first season, fans actually got their first full look at Korra following the events of her series.

Avatar: Seven Havens ended its first season with a tease of what happened to Korra towards the end of her time as the Avatar, and came with some other surprises to fans. Not only did it seem like Korra and Asami got married in the years after The Legend of Korra , but Asami was nowhere to be seen when Korra seemingly led to the destruction of the world. But speaking with IGN , Avatar: Seven Havens co-creator Michael DiMartino and executive producer Sehaj Sethi confirmed that Asami is indeed dead, “Asami is definitely dead by our show, which I think is a fair thing to say.”

Avatar: Seven Havens Producers Confirm Asami Is Dead

“Asami is definitely dead by our show, which I think is a fair thing to say,” Sehaj stated when asked about the Korra and Asami tease near the end of Avatar: Seven Havens ‘ debut season. This really shouldn’t come as a surprise considering that there were hundreds of years following the end of The Legend of Korra , and there’s no way she would have survived until the sequel series. But thankfully, Sehaj also teases that her fate comes after a time jump of years after the end of that series .

“The main thing to know from that is that there is most likely a time jump,” and the producer further teased we’ll find out more about Korra and Asami’s future in the coming season, “But as to their relationship, you do learn more about that in Season 2.” This was further confirmed by co-creator Michael DiMartino who revealed that we will see more of their past relationship in future episodes as well. Because while the two of them were married, Korra doesn’t wear the betrothal necklace when she seemingly causes the cataclysm . This might be setting up some unfortunate end for their romance too.

What Happens With Korra and Asami After The Legend of Korra ?

Avatar: Seven Havens has begun to fill in the gaps of Korra’s past after The Legend of Korra, and we’ll see all of this develop further in the future episodes. One of the main complaints from the end of that series was that Korra and Asami couldn’t fully confirm their romantic connection on screen, and it took the creators going to social media afterwards to outright state it themselves . But that’s no longer going to be the case with this new era of the franchise.

If Avatar: Seven Havens dives further into their future in the coming seasons , then it’s going to be a great way for the franchise to sort of make amends for the way that The Legend of Korra ended while telling its own new story. But we’ll just have to see what’s next for the duo and whether or not they got their happy ending before Asami’s death. What do you want to see from them in the future? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

HT – IGN

title: Black Clover Season 2 Dominates Crunchyroll’s Fall 2026 Schedule With New Streaming Milestone
content:
It turns out Black Clover has been absolutely dominating Crunchyroll’s new slate of Fall 2026 anime releases as it has hit a new streaming milestone for October. This past October kicked off a new wave of anime that began their runs for the Fall, and the season has been largely dominated by returning franchises coming back for new episodes . But even with all of that competition, it’s been made clear that there’s one returning franchise in particular that fans have been most anticipating this Fall.

Black Clover has returned for Season 2 of the anime series five years after fans had been left waiting on a cliffhanger with the first season, and there’s been an explosive response to it all thus far. As revealed by the official social media account for the series, Black Clover Season 2 was the top most watched anime on Crunchyroll through the month of October. That’s especially impressive when you consider the worldwide reach of the streaming service, and is a good sign for the end of the year.

Black Clover Season 2 Takes Top Spot on Crunchyroll October 2026 Charts

Black Clover Season 2 was the most anticipated anime franchise return of the year overall. With Yuki Tabata’s original manga series ending its own 11 year run earlier this Spring, this meant that the anime was going to be the only new release that fans could look forward to. Picking up from a massive cliffhanger it left off of five years ago , shooting to the top of the charts like this has further proven that there was a ton of fans eagerly waiting to see what was next, and even more so for those who have not kept up with the anime.

Black Clover Season 2 picks up with its adaptation of the Spade Kingdom Raid arc from Yuki Tabata’s original manga. Following a few days of training, the Clover Kingdom’s Magic Knights have come to the Spade Kingdom to stop the Dark Triad’s Advent of Qliphoth ritual before Yami and Vangeance are sacrificed. I t’s been nonstop action through all of the episodes thus far as well , so that’s also a good reason as to why it’s been such a hit for Crunchyroll with only a few episodes into its run thus far.

How Long Is Black Clover Season 2 Going to Be?

Black Clover Season 2 has yet to confirm how many episodes it’s going to be running for, but it’s likely only going to be a single cour of 12 or 13 episodes at the current rate the anime is going. The chapters from this arc weren’t really that long to begin with, and also have a ton of action that will likely go much quicker in the anime than they did in the original pages. But at the same time, the team behind it a ll has really gone all out for the biggest moments of each fight seen so far .

Regardless, it’s not going to be anywhere near as long as the 170 episode heavy first season . With only two arcs left from Black Clover’ s manga overall, the anime is likely going to come to an end much quicker than fans might be hoping for. And when that happens, expect the anime to break even more records with Crunchyroll. How are you liking Black Clover Season 2 so far? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

title: Pokémon Pokopia Game Adds Expansion Pass DLC Part 2 'Dazzling Decorations' on December 9
content:
The official X/Twitter account for the Pokémon franchise announced on Wednesday that the second part of the paid Expansion Pass DLC for Pokémon Pokopia , its cozy-style life simulation crafting game for the Pokémon franchise , will launch on December 9.

The second DLC part includes accessories such as sunglasses, Sylveon ribbon, and bow tie. The DLC will also include Doduo, Skitty, Braixen, and more Pokémon.

The game's paid Expansion Pass DLC added the underwater Bubbly Basin town on August 5 as part 1 of the pass, and it will add another town in 2027 as part 3. Purchasing the DLC gives players a bonus Dynamic Ditto print recipe and bonus Rare Pokémetal in-game. The free update that launched with part 1 of the DLC included new Pokémon such as Manaphy, Popplio, Mudkip, Chinchou, Lanturn, Buizel, Corphish, Totodile, Dhelmise, Golisopod, Corsola, Frillish, Lumineon, and Sharpedo. A free update added the ability for players to explore and build underwater in existing towns using the new ability to Dive.

The game launched for Nintendo Switch 2 on March 5 with a Game-Key Card release. Game-Key Cards are physical cartridges that do not actually contain a game, but rather, a key to unlock and play the digital version from Nintendo 's eShop. Koei Tecmo developed the game. Nintendo and The Pokémon Company announced in August the game has sold more than 5 million units worldwide in about four months.

title: Blue Eye Samurai Creators Address the Long Wait for Season 2’s Release
content:
Blue Eye Samurai is finally coming back to Netflix for its second season early next year, and the creators behind the anime inspired animated series have addressed fans who have been waiting four years to see the new episodes in action. Blue Eye Samurai was a breakout success with the streaming service when it originally made its debut in 2023 , and went on to win major Emmy Awards and more in the time since. But its next season has been in development for quite a while.

Blue Eye Samurai Season 2 is now on track to release with Netflix in January 202 7, and series creators Amber Noizumi and Michael Green opened up to Netflix’s Tudum about the wait and thanked fans for their patience, “First, we want to thank all of our viewers for waiting,” the creators stated. “Your enthusiasm is what energized us and helped us get here.” The two of them also teased a bit of what’s coming in the new season and its new location .

Why Blue Eye Samurai Season 2 Took Three Years to Develop

“Rome wasn’t built in a day, and neither were 17th-century London or Edo Japan,” Blue Eye Samurai co-creators Noizumi and Green said about the four year wait in between the first and second seasons. “The care that every single member of our team poured into researching those worlds, then crafting them brushstroke by brushstroke into breathtaking, moving art is nothing short of a miracle to us.” But that development time makes a lot of sense when you consider that Season 2 is heading to a whole new region for its story.

Following the end of the first season , Mizu is heading to London which is teased by the duo as “a thriving culture of illicit activity.” Mizu is going to be navigating through a “dark underbelly amid a puritanical society that persecuted women as witches, closed bars and theaters, and even outlawed Christmas.” Following through on the themes seen in the first season, Mizu is going to be dealing with oppression on a different scale, “For the first time, she’ll have to confront what it’s like to stand out as Asian in a sea of white faces,” the creators tease. “And then find out what it means to be a woman during one of the most oppressive times in English history.”

When Does Blue Eye Samurai Season 2 Come Out?

Blue Eye Samurai Season 2 will be making its worldwide debut with Netflix on January 19th next year with co-creators Amber Noizumi and Michael Green also serving as writers and executive producers. Erwin Stoff serves as an executive producer with Jane Wu as supervising director and producer with animation produced by Blue Spirit much like the first season. Confirmed returning cast members include Maya Erskine as Mizu, Brenda Song as Akemi, Darren Barnet as Taigen, Masi Oka as Ringo, and Kenneth Branagh as Abijah Fowler.

New additions to the voice cast for Season 2 include Jonathan Pryce as Old Violet, Joel Kim Booster as Priest Ando, and Sherry Cola as Kuma, but their exact roles in the story have yet to be divulged at this time. Though there might have been a gap between the first and second seasons, it won’t be the same for the third as it will be slated for a release soon after in 2028. Serving as the final season for the series overall , Blue Eye Samurai fans have a lot to look forward to.

How are you feeling about the wait for Blue Eye Samurai Season 2? Are you excited to see more of Mizu at last? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

title: Reincarnated as a Sword Season 2 Anime Reveals Trailer, Visual, Cast for Seedrun Arc
content:
The official website for the television anime of Yuu Tanaka and LLO 's Reincarnated as a Sword ( Tensei Shitara Ken Deshita ) light novel series revealed on Thursday a new trailer, visual, and additional cast for the Seedrun Arc of the anime's second season .

The newly announced cast members include:

The new arc begins with the sixth episode.

Itsuki Fujioka (romanization of manga creator's name is unconfirmed) launched a manga spinoff for the franchise titled Tensei Shitara Ken Deshita My Dish on Micro Magazine 's Comic Ride service on September 30.

HIDIVE is streaming the anime as it airs in Japan, and it screened the North American premiere of the new season on August 22 at Anime NYC .

The company describes the anime:

Reincarnated as a sentient weapon with memories of his past life, but not his name, a magical sword saves a young beastgirl from a life of slavery. Fran, the cat-eared girl, becomes his wielder, and wants only to grow stronger, while the sword wants to know why he is here. Together, the strange duo's journey has only just begun!

The first anime season premiered on Tokyo MX in October 2022 before airing on ABC TV and BS Asahi . Episodes debuted a week early ABEMA service, starting in September 2022. HIDIVE streamed the anime as it aired and also streamed an English dub .

The series stars Ai Kakuma as Fran, Shinichirō Miki as Master, and Yūma Uchida as Jean du Vix.

Shinji Ishihira ( Fairy Tail , Log Horizon , Edens Zero ) returns to direct the anime at at C2C . Takahiro Nagano ( Duel Masters script writer) is writing and supervising the scripts. Atsuko Saitō ( Hitori Bocchi no Marumaru Seikatsu , Wandering Witch - The Journey of Elaina episode animation director) designs the characters. Yasuharu Takanashi is composing the music.

Additional staff members include:

• Assistant director: Kazunobu Shimizu

• Master design: Shinya Asanuma

• Monster design: Chie Sakurai, Jumpei Mukai, Shōta Yano

• Action director: Rino Isago, Satoshi Sakai, Shunya Nitta

• Color key artist: Masato Takagi, Takeshi Kurihara

• Art director/setting: Masahiro Satō

• Art board: Kōki Nagayoshi

• Prop design: Tomoki Yokoyama, Emi Kōno

• Compositing director of photography: Masaaki Onodera

• 3DCG: Hinokuni Animation

• 2D/Monitor works: Jumpei Mukai

• Editing: Gō Sadamatsu

• Music director: Shōji Hata

FZMZ performs the opening theme song "Dream of Butterfly" and Hanabie. performs the ending theme song "Baribari Buddy."

Tanaka launched the novels on the Shōsetsuka ni Narou website in October 2015, and Gentosha began publishing the series with illustrations by LLO in July 2016. Tomowo Maruyama launched a manga adaptation of the novels on Gentosha 's Denshi Birz website in December 2016. Seven Seas Entertainment is releasing both the original light novels and Maruyama's manga adaptation in English. The company also launched audiobooks of the novels narrated by Josh Hurley in August 2024.

Hinako Inoue launched the Tensei Shitara Ken Deshita: Another Wish manga spinoff in June 2020 and ended it in its sixth compiled book volume in March 2023.

title: Yu-Gi-Oh Drops First Look at New 30th Anniversary Artbook Release
content:
Yu-Gi-Oh! has kicked off a new era of the franchise 30 years after its original debut with Shueisha’s Weekly Shonen Jump magazine, and the series has dropped the first look at a cool new art book coming soon to help celebrate. The late Kazuki Takahashi’s original series might have made its debut looking a lot differently than what it looked like when it came to an end, and that just also goes to show the strength of Takahashi’s art over the series’ many years. Not to even mention all of the sequels and spinoffs released since.

Yu-Gi-Oh! likely has a lot more planned for the franchise’s 30th anniversary , but Shonen Jump is helping to kick things off on a strong foot with the launch of a new digital art book coming later this month in Japan. As spotted by @WSJ_manga on X , this new Yu-Gi-Oh! digital art book will feature 200 color illustrations from Takahashi’s time with the series and includes an awesome cover to boot. You can check out cover below ahead of the new book’s upcoming release.

What’s Next for Yu-Gi-Oh ‘s 30th Anniversary?

Kazuki Takahashi’s Yu-Gi-Oh! originally made its debut with Shueisha’s Weekly Shonen Jump magazine in September 1996, and ran for nearly a decade. To help celebrate its original debut, the franchise will be launching a special exhibition “YU-GI-OH! ART WORKS” later this December in Japan. This exhibition will be showcasing a much closer look at Takahashi’s work with the franchise over the years, and will be yet another way that fans can celebrate just how far it’s all come. It even got a special anime trailer for the occasion too.

Yu-Gi-Oh! originally started out as a much darker series where the Pharaoh pit his opponents against deadly games that were much more intense than the card games that the series would later be known for. This shift in the series ended up making the manga even more of a breakout success in its later years that resulted in multiple video games, a real life trading card game, and sparked a franchise of new sequels and spinoffs that would continue to reboot itself for decades to come after it all. It was quite a pivot.

Will Yu-Gi-Oh ‘s Anime Ever Get a Reboot?

Despite how many sequels and spinoffs that Yu-Gi-Oh! has had ever since the end of its original series, there’s still a desire to see the most classic version of the franchise return for its own reboot someday. With so many other classic hits making their returns decades later with brand new revivals introducing their stories to fans of the modern era, this desire for a reboot has gotten even stronger with recent remasters of sequels that came after like with Yu-Gi-Oh! GX (which unfortunately only released in Japan ).

With Konami continuing to release new anime and more for the franchise in the decades since the original series, it really does seem like a revival or reboot of the classic series (perhaps even being more faithful to Takahashi’s manga) would be potentially on the table. But would you want to see a reboot of the classic Yu-Gi-Oh! anime? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

HT – @WSJ_manga on X
